data.summary: This 7‑week plan starts with the student’s weak units, interleaves new material, and ends with a mixed review and timed practice. Each week uses the 8 available hours, includes concrete tasks, and only recommends live classes that match the week’s topics.

weeks.focus: Master the fundamentals of differentiation and review limits.
tasks: Read and summarize the definitions in 1.2 and 1.3, then solve 5 limit problems with graph and table methods.
Do 10 derivative practice problems covering 2.1 and 2.2, marking each against the scoring guide.

weeks.focus: Apply derivative rules and deepen limit understanding.
tasks: Estimate limits from tables in 1.4 and solve 5 algebraic limit problems in 1.5.
Complete 10 problems on estimating derivatives (2.3) and 5 power‑rule problems (2.5), recording solutions and errors.
Solve 8 chain‑rule problems (3.1) and 6 implicit‑differentiation problems (3.2).
Tackle 4 inverse‑function differentiation problems (3.3) and review solutions.

weeks.focus: Connect derivatives to real‑world motion and rates.
tasks: Attend live class on 4.1 and 4.2. After class, do 5 motion‑based word problems (4.2) and 5 rate‑change problems (4.3).

weeks.focus: Use the first derivative to analyze functions.
tasks: Apply the Mean Value Theorem to 4 functions (5.1).
Identify critical points and classify them using EVT and the first derivative test (5.2, 5.3).

weeks.focus: Build integration skills and revisit accumulation concepts.
tasks: Attend live class covering 6.1 and 6.2. Post‑class, complete 5 Riemann sum approximations (6.2) and 3 definite integral problems (6.3).

weeks.focus: Mixed review and timed practice for exam readiness.
tasks: Do a 60‑minute timed practice test covering all units. Then review 10 challenging problems from each of the listed topics, focusing on common pitfalls.

data.final_week_advice: In the final week, prioritize full-length timed practice and targeted review of weak spots identified during the plan. Focus on pacing, error analysis, and reinforcing conceptual understanding before the exam.
